title: Fix: pouring data not reaching cloud for ~8 days (missing heat-cycle bridge call)
description: Root cause: PouringProcessor._sync_mould_records_to_heat_cycle() (the bridge that populates heat_cycles.pouring_start_time/pouring_end_time/mould_wise_pouring_time via HeatCycleManager.upsert_completed_mould_pouring) is never called from production code - only from a unit test. Every heat cycle since 2026-07-30 19:44:43 (HEAT_1481 onward) has finalized with blank pouring aggregates even though individual pours are detected fine and sit in pouring_events. sync_manager.py silently skips these as 'incomplete sessions' (logger.debug only) and marks them synced=1 anyway because melting/tapping sync succeeds - zero errors logged anywhere. Predates this week's mould-selection/clustering-removal work (not a regression from that). Plan: (1) wire the missing call into _end_pour's committed_tracker_id block, (2) add has_pouring_session as a persisted heat_cycles column + sync_manager hardening to log an error if has_pouring_session=true but pouring_start_time is blank, (3) one-off dry-run-first backfill script reconstructing the ~8 days of affected heat cycles from pouring_events and resending just the pouring payload.
close_reason: Root cause: hicon-1lm (2026-07-31) gated legacy clustering functions behind mould_count_mode != tracker to stop wasted compute, but _close_active_mould was also the only production caller of _sync_mould_records_to_heat_cycle() (the bridge feeding heat_cycles.pouring_start_time/pouring_end_time/mould_wise_pouring_time, which the cloud /pouring payload is built from). Gating off the wasteful call site silently cut off the only functional one too - pours kept recording fine in pouring_events, they just never reached the heat-cycle aggregate, and sync_manager silently skipped (debug only) + marked synced=1 anyway since /agni succeeded. Fixed: (1) call the bridge directly from _end_pour's tracker-commit block, (2) persisted has_pouring_session on heat_cycles + sync_manager now logs an ERROR (routes to Sentry) if a real pouring session's aggregate comes out empty instead of silently skipping, (3) new regression test drives a real _end_pour through a real HeatCycleManager (existing tests only ever called the bridge directly, never through _end_pour - exactly how this escaped the suite), (4) backfill script (tools/backfill_heat_cycle_pouring.py) reconstructed and resent all 54 affected historical heat cycles from pouring_events - 0 failures, verified against DB. Committed+pushed as ed25f3e. hicon-vision.service still needs a manual restart (no sudo access in this session) to deploy the forward-looking fix - user will do this themselves.

title: Camera LAN periodic outage: all 3 RTSP streams cut ~40-55s on ~298.5s cycle
description: Live-captured 2026-07-18: synchronized data loss on all 3 streams (12:15:19/12:20:19/12:25:19/12:30:19 grid, period 298.5s). Per-source staggered recoveries 40/50/55s prove genuine camera-side outage, not mux artifact. Camera 0 (28.119) additionally goes L3 ping-dead ~49s after the cut (firmware network-stack bounce, same signature as June 12 investigation). WAN/tailscale unaffected during cuts => camera switch segment or camera-side mass event, NOT Jetson NIC or router port. ~250 stalls/day per stream since Jul 15. One watchdog escalation crash Jul 16 01:08 (stream 2 stale 300s). Suspects: camera PoE switch uplink flap, or NVR-triggered mass session kill, or all-3 camera firmware cycle. Gateways: cam0=28.8(alive), cam1/2=28.200 (ICMP-dead, ARP-alive). Ping monitors + auto-analyzer left running 2026-07-18 12:38-13:38.
notes: CONCLUSIVE (2026-07-18 12:40 & 12:45 windows, live ping monitors): during each stall, ALL of 192.168.28.x dropped ping simultaneously — cam0 (28.119) gap 20.5s/35.8s, cam1 (28.172) 21.5s/33.3s, cam2 (28.174) 21.0s/35.9s(+35.8s), NVR-1 (28.8) 16.9s/10.2s — while router gateway 192.168.175.200 had ZERO gaps through the same Jetson NIC. => The entire 28.x segment loses connectivity on the ~298.5s grid (12:40:1x, 12:45:1x); Jetson port and router are healthy. NVR recovers ~15-25s before the cameras each time — consistent with cameras hanging off the NVR/PoE switch one hop deeper, or slower camera-side recovery. Root cause is the switch/uplink feeding the 28.x devices (likely NVR/camera PoE switch). Fix: inspect/replace that switch or its uplink; check whether cameras are on NVR PoE ports; check switch logs/power. Pipeline code is NOT at fault; watchdog escalation (Jul 16 01:08 exit) was correct behavior.
close_reason: Duplicate of hicon-b22 (same Jul-15-onset ~300s storm). All evidence from 2026-07-18 instrumentation (per-session 298s TTL, selective ICMP blackouts, simultaneous Jul-12 camera reboots, mux-artifact rulled out, switch-cut hypothesis REVISED to stateful-middlebox) recorded in hicon-b22 notes.

title: Fix mould slot-number collisions and orphaned heat-cycle records
description: Two bugs from one trigger (canonical merge of two moulds that had each already poured), both corrupting heat_cycles mould counts. (A) UNDERCOUNT: MOULD_C{n} labels are derived as len(_tracker_slot_by_id)+1 in _end_pour; _merge_canonical discards the dropped ID's slot when the survivor already has one, so the dict shrinks and the next new tracker ID re-derives the freed number. upsert_completed_mould_pouring matches on the mould_id STRING, so two distinct moulds sharing a label collapse into one record. Confirmed in HEAT_1540: tracker IDs 1229+1230 both slot_id=6, slots 3/4 absent. (B) OVERCOUNT + double-counted duration: cycle.mould_pourings is only ever appended to (no removal path anywhere) and _merge_canonical never notifies HeatCycleManager, so a merged-away mould's record is orphaned in the cycle forever while its duration is also folded into the survivor's total. Fix A: monotonic _next_tracker_slot counter (+ seed from max() in _restore_tracker_state_from_heat_cycle for mid-cycle restarts, + reset in _reset_all_state). Fix B: add HeatCycleManager.prune_tracker_mould_pourings() and make _sync_mould_records_to_heat_cycle reconcile (upsert + prune) against _tracker_pour_records. Only manifests on the live path, which started working at ed25f3e (14:27 2026-08-07).
close_reason: Fixed both bugs. (A) UNDERCOUNT: replaced the len(_tracker_slot_by_id)+1 slot derivation in _end_pour with a monotonic _next_tracker_slot counter, seeded past restored slots in _restore_tracker_state_from_heat_cycle (mid-cycle restart would otherwise renumber from 1 and re-collide) and reset per heat cycle. Stops a merge-freed number being handed to a different physical mould, which upsert_completed_mould_pouring then collapsed into one record since it matches on the mould_id string. (B) OVERCOUNT + double-counted duration: added HeatCycleManager.prune_tracker_mould_pourings() and made _sync_mould_records_to_heat_cycle reconcile (upsert + prune) against _tracker_pour_records, removing merged-away moulds whose records previously survived forever. 4 regression tests added, each VERIFIED to fail against pre-fix code (assert 3==4 for reused slot, assert 1==6 for restart counter, orphaned MOULD_C3 retained). Suite 147 passed (2 pre-existing unrelated segment_buffer_helper failures). Committed 55bc1fe (bundled with a parallel decoupled-analysis-topology removal that was in the working tree), pushed, and deployed via service restart 16:35:41 IST - all 3 streams at 25fps, zero errors. Note: no historical backfill - the 54 already-sent cycles had correct counts (tracker-id-keyed), only duplicate labels which cannot be retroactively disambiguated.

title: Investigate Stream 0 mux-upscale deadlock and review root-cause chain
description: Run faithful baseline and native/non-upscaled Stream 0 DeepStream comparisons for nvosd_0/libnvbufsurftransform deadlock, preserve logs, revert experiment, and independently audit ai_vision/docs/rtsp_stream0_investigation.md against current code/config/evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline and no-upscale paths are exercised or hardware limitation is explicit; evidence is captured; temporary config is reverted; causal claims are tagged confirmed/hypothesis with file/log grounding.
notes: EXPERIMENT COMPLETE 2026-08-03 14:17-14:34 IST. Actual Stream0 mux config is ai_vision/.env HICON_STREAM_0_MUX_WIDTH/HEIGHT -> config.py:215-217 -> hicon_pipeline.py:1696-1697 -> gst_builder.py:1161-1165/_create_streammux:364-378. Camera 2688x1520 to mux 1600x900 is a downscale/rescale, not an upscale. Baseline 1600x900: pipeline.log:90011-90015 showed upstream/caps stages fresh while preosdq_src aged 4.03->9.03s and output 0fps; at 90342-90349 it reached preosdq 319.03s and watchdog restarted. Native 2688x1520: config confirmed at pipeline.log:91088-91089; after a brief all-camera startup network interruption, Stream0 recovered upstream. pipeline.log:91244-91251 showed mux through caps fresh <=0.05s while preosdq aged 44.04->49.04s and output 0fps; 91504-91537 showed same through 299.04s; 91570 watchdog restarted at 300s. On-disk config was restored before experiment ended; replacement process confirmed 1600x900 at 91703-91704. Temporary timer code/env removed. Conclusion: mux rescaling is ruled out as a necessary trigger, high confidence (same deterministic failure signature and full watchdog cycle). No nvosd bus error or NvBufSurfTransform log/backtrace was captured; sandbox PID namespace/ptrace prevented gdb attach, so libnvbufsurftransform attribution remains hypothesis. Validation: py_compile passed; focused tests passed 30/30 with PYTHONPATH set.

title: Gate legacy clustering mould-count path behind non-tracker modes
description: Legacy spatial-clustering mould counting (_open_active_mould/_close_active_mould/_materialize_mould_records/_build_clusters etc. in ai_vision/processors/pouring_processor.py) runs unconditionally every pour regardless of MOULD_COUNT_MODE, even though live .env has MOULD_COUNT_MODE=tracker. Its output still feeds the DB 'moulds' breakdown (_get_mould_breakdown) and the live inference/MJPEG overlays, so users still see old clustering-derived data even in tracker mode. Fix: gate all legacy compute (including MouldPlacementDetector predictive lifecycle calls) to only run when mould_count_mode != 'tracker'; build a tracker-based per-mould breakdown for the DB 'moulds' field and repoint overlays to tracker data when mode==tracker; delete confirmed-dead-in-all-modes constants (MOULD_SPLIT_*, MOULD_SWITCH_MIN_POUR_S, _dominant_axis). Keep legacy/shadow modes intact as rollback per user decision. Reference implementation validated against soumyadipbhattacharyya/HI-CON yolo_mould branch (pure NvDCF-tracker-ID mould counting, no clustering).
notes:
Implemented via targeted gating rather than deletion (per user decision to keep legacy/shadow as rollback):
- _start_pour/_end_pour: _open_active_mould, _close_active_mould, and MouldPlacementDetector lifecycle calls now skip when mould_count_mode=='tracker'; unchanged in legacy/shadow.
- _get_mould_breakdown() now dispatches to new _get_tracker_mould_breakdown() (built from self._tracker_pour_records) in tracker mode, instead of always reading legacy self.mould_records. This is the field written into the DB mould_wise_pouring_time.moulds payload.
- _add_inference_display_meta (nvosd overlay) and draw_cpu_overlay (MJPEG overlay) now show tracker-derived counts/per-mould rows in tracker mode instead of frozen/stale legacy fields.
- Canonical mould registry, EMA trolley smoothing, majority-vote assignment, trolley-handoff detection all left untouched (kept per user decision - they compensate for real Jetson interval-based inference ID churn that the simpler yolo_mould reference app doesn't need to handle).
- Added 2 regression tests confirming tracker mode skips legacy compute while shadow mode still runs it, and that the DB breakdown is tracker-sourced in tracker mode.
- Did NOT delete the confirmed-dead-in-all-modes MOULD_SPLIT_*/MOULD_SWITCH_MIN_POUR_S config constants (flagged in inventory as safe cleanup but out of scope for this fix — separate low-risk follow-up if wanted).
- Verified: full ai_vision test suite passes (149 passed, 1 skipped) aside from 3 pre-existing unrelated failures (segment_buffer_helper, stream0_local_relay) confirmed present on main before this change too.
close_reason: Legacy clustering path gated behind mould_count_mode != 'tracker'; DB breakdown and overlays repointed to tracker data in tracker mode; legacy/shadow modes preserved as rollback; tests added and full suite green

title: Harden Hicon direct RTSP recovery for all three cameras
description: Keep all Hicon sources on direct camera RTSP, reduce reconnect tails, isolate per-stream failures, and verify live recovery without NVR dependency. Root network outages remain tracked in hicon-b22.
acceptance_criteria: All three direct RTSP streams recover independently after camera reachability returns; no healthy-stream pipeline restart; 25 FPS during healthy periods; unit/config tests pass; production service verification recorded.
notes:
2026-07-24 deployed direct-camera RTSP mitigation on Hicon: HICON_RTSP_PROTOCOL_0/1/2 changed from forced tcp to auto (nvurisrcbin rtp-multi, UDP-first with TCP fallback), latency remains 2000ms, reconnect 2s/unlimited. Controlled six-puller test: all 3 TCP pulls closed together at 12:15:34 while UDP pulls remained open; production socket inspection confirmed UDP RTP/RTCP pairs. Live event at 12:19 showed actual all-stream source loss still exists upstream: UDP reduced recoveries to stream2 15s, stream0 30s versus prior TCP 35-40s; no whole-pipeline restart. Post-recovery 24.6-25.2fps each; isolated stream0 blip recovered in 2.1s without affecting healthy streams. Jetson NIC remained 1Gb full duplex/carrier-up, no kernel link/driver/OOM/thermal event. Temporary hicon-rtsp-probe stopped to free session. Focused RTSP tests 22 passed. Remaining physical/shared camera-segment outage stays in hicon-b22.
CORRECTION after second live boundary: UDP-first/auto failed production acceptance and was rolled back to forced TCP at 12:26. Second event at 12:24:14 caused stream2 43.9s loss then repeated flapping; after fresh forced-TCP restart camera2 192.168.28.174 itself remained ICMP-dead and port 554 timed out while cameras0/1 were reachable and 25fps. Therefore no UDP-first mitigation is claimed as deployed. Production is restored to the prior TCP baseline. Issue blocked on shared camera network/PoE path repair tracked by hicon-b22.

title: Build hicon-timeline: NVR gap-free delayed re-stream service
description: Additive standalone service (timeline_service.py + pipeline/nvr_timeline_helper.py) that continuously republishes NVR 192.168.28.6 footage (tracks 1201/901/1301) into a dedicated MediaMTX instance (port 8555), delayed ~205s behind live, with a capture-clock anchor (anchor.json: capture_epoch/host_monotonic/rate) so downstream event timestamps can reflect original capture time regardless of buffering/backfill lag. Does NOT touch hicon_pipeline.py/hicon-vision.service/gst_builder.py/config.py — the live direct-camera pipeline is completely unmodified. Pointing the existing pipeline at this timeline's output (HICON_RTSP_STREAM_x -> rtsp://127.0.0.1:8555/timelineN) and wiring the capture-clock into _ProbeTimestampResolver are separate, later, explicit follow-up steps. Resource-driven design choice: Jetson only has ~3.6GB free RAM, so this must NOT run a second full DeepStream/TensorRT pipeline -- it produces plain re-muxed video only. Spike doc: ai_vision/docs/nvr_backfill_feasibility_2026-07-23.md
notes:
INCIDENT: Part 2 cutover attempted 2026-07-25 11:34 IST, rolled back 11:43 IST (9 min).

What happened: pointed hicon-vision.service at hicon-timeline (rtsp://127.0.0.1:8555/timelineN) + HICON_DELAYED_CAPTURE_CLOCK=true, restarted. Streams 0 and 2 immediately began dropping to 0fps and reconnecting every ~6-8s (6 outages each in the first 96s; stream 1 had 0). Timeline's own state.json showed no rebuffering during this window, ruling out the timeline running dry.

Root cause (suspected, not yet confirmed): nvurisrcbin's aggressive 'no data >2s' watchdog reacting to momentary delivery-rate jitter in the timeline's republished stream. title: fix: nvurisrcbin FPS watchdog restart corrupts vsrc_0 pad, stalling stream 0 permanently
description: The 90s FPS watchdog calls schedule_stream_restart() on nvurisrcbin (stream 0). Cycling nvurisrcbin through NULL does not clean its dynamic vsrc_0 pad, so when it returns to PLAYING GStreamer emits 'Padname vsrc_0 is not unique'. Fix: skip the NULL→PLAYING state cycle for nvurisrcbin streams; let built-in reconnect handle drops. Escalate to full service restart (loop.quit) only after 300s.

Actual root cause: camera 0's default gateway was set to 192.168.28.1 which DOES NOT EXIST on the network (ARP incomplete forever). Hikvision firmware's periodic gateway health check failed every cycle and its recovery action bounced the camera's network/streaming stack every ~298.5s (free-running timer), silently killing all RTSP sessions (later RST win0 = TCP state lost), with 0-9s ICMP/HTTP blip. Camera OS never rebooted (uptime 5.6d). Controls: identical cameras 1&2 (same model/firmware) point at gateway 192.168.27.1 which EXISTS and never cycled. Also explains why replacing CP Plus with Hikvision didn't help (same dead gateway on 28.x). The old '95s TCP refusal' no longer applied by June (new TCP accepted within seconds). FIX (2026-06-12 19:09): gateway changed to 192.168.28.8 (NVR-1, always-on, answers ARP) via ISAPI PUT + camera reboot. Verification: watch [RTSP-OUTAGE] in pipeline.log for 30+ min.

rtspsrc path for stream 0 (HICON_USE_NVURISRCBIN_0=false) crashes with pgie-pouring: not-negotiated when first frame arrives from camera (~1.3s after PLAYING). Root cause: nvtracker rejects dynamic CAPS event during PLAYING state — caps on pgie_pouring→tracker_0 link aren't pre-established before data flows, unlike nvurisrcbin where vsrc_0 pad connects during PAUSED→PLAYING. Confirmed by: bypass tracker → no crash. Attempted fixes that failed: (1) deep-element-added to set do-rtsp-keep-alive on internal src element (ignored by nvurisrcbin), (2) batched-push-timeout=30s (irrelevant, crash is on first real frame not empty batch), (3) capsfilter(NV12+1600x900) between pgie and tracker (breaks displayq0→nvosd_0 link), (4) capsfilter(NV12 only) between pgie and tracker (same link failure). Next approach: use nvvideoconvert between caps0 and premuxq0 to output RGBA and match standard DeepStream sample pipeline topology, OR send RECONFIGURE event on tracker sink pad after PLAYING.
